subject: Proposal: Reserved GPU pool uplift + SLA credits for renewal
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Samir Rao <samir@avatech.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 2 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal + uplift proposal: reserved GPU pool increase and SLA credits

Hi Samir,

Hope you had a good weekend. As Ava's annual renewal window approaches (your account is set to renew 2025-12-01), we ran the utilization forecast and recommend a reserved pool uplift to avoid throttling during your marketing peak in Jan–Mar. The proposed change: add 24x A100-equivalent GPUs to your Dedicated pool (from 48 -> 72), keep the current burst arrangement, and extend the term to 18 months to lock preferential rates.

We understand the uplift changes the availability risk profile for Redwood. To address your procurement and risk team, we've attached a short addendum that outlines an SLA exception package:
- Adjusted p99 latency target for high-throughput batch windows (60ms -> 75ms)
- 30% uptime credit buffer for scheduling conflicts tied to capacity rebalancing during the first 90 days
- Prioritized capacity scaling window for scheduled events (48h notice)

Attached: redwood_uplift_proposal_v3.pdf (proposal) and a draft SLA exception term sheet. If this aligns with your expectations, we can circulate a redline and route for signature.

Available times for a 30-min call this week: Tue 11/4 10:00–12:00 PT or Thu 11/6 14:00–16:00 PT.

Thanks — looking forward to your thoughts.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0183
From: Samir Rao <samir@avatech.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@avatech.com>, Procurement <procurement@avatech.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Nov 2025 11:08:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Renewal + uplift proposal: reserved GPU pool increase and SLA credits

Kim — thanks for the clear proposal. The architecture team flagged that we will likely need the extra capacity for our Q1 generative campaigns; finance is OK with the term extension if the unit economics hold. A couple of questions before we schedule: 

1) The p99 latency delta — can you explain how that maps to our SLIs (specifically for interactive chat endpoints vs. batch inference)? We need to be sure chat latency isn't materially affected.
2) The 30% uptime credit buffer sounds reasonable, but procurement wants the exact credit calculation. Is it linear or a stepped credit depending on breach severity?

If you can send a short note answering the two points I can get procurement to prioritize. Tentatively Thu 11/6 14:00 PT works for a call.

—Samir
Chief ML Officer
Ava Technologies
samir@avatech.com
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Nov 2025 08:35:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal + uplift proposal: internal SLO clarifications for Ava uplift

Kim / Marissa — following Samir's questions, I pulled the SLO matrix and drafted suggested language for the two bullets:

- p99 latency: separate baseline targets for real-time chat routes (p95 <= 120ms, p99 <= 220ms) versus batch generation routes (p95 <= 140ms, p99 <= 400ms). The proposed 75ms shift should apply only to the batch profile during the first 60 days while caches and shard warming complete.
- uptime credits: propose a stepped credit schedule: 10% credit for availability between 99.0–99.5%, 25% for 98.0–99.0%, 50% below 98.0% for the uplifts window (first 90 days). After 90 days revert to the standard contract credits.

Also, recommend we include a one-time operational support credit (8 hours pooled CS/Eng escalation support) to help their on-call during the migration week. Attaching the redline I plan to send to Samir.

Ben
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Samir Rao <samir@avatech.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@avatech.com>
Date: Thu, 6 Nov 2025 14:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal + uplift proposal: reserved GPU pool increase and SLA credits

Samir — thanks for the quick reply and for locking the call. Short answers below and I've pasted Ben's recommended language for contract clarity.

1) Chat vs batch: Our routing and model-profiles already separate interactive chat traffic onto lower-latency lanes; the 75ms relaxed p99 applies exclusively to batch-generation profiles (offline jobs and large-batch scoring). Interactive chat SLOs will remain at or below current published targets.

2) Credits: We propose a stepped credit schedule (see Ben's draft below). The calculation is percentage-of-monthly-reserved-fee applied pro rata for the affected billing month. If you prefer a single blended credit we can produce that number for procurement.

---- Forwarded draft language from Ben Carter ----
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Nov 2025 08:35:00 -0800

- Batch profile p99 target adjustment: During the first 60 days after capacity activation, batch-generation routes will have adjusted p99 target = published_p99 + 75ms. Interactive/chat routes unaffected.
- Uptime credit schedule for uplift period (first 90 days):
    • 99.5%–100%: no credit
    • 99.0%–99.5%: 10% credit of monthly reserved pool fee
    • 98.0%–99.0%: 25% credit
    • <98.0%: 50% credit + escalation review
- One-time operational support: 8 hours of pooled escalation time (CS + Infra) during the initial migration week.

---- end draft ----

If that looks reasonable, I'll have legal prepare a short addendum and return with a DocuSign packet. We can also include explicit examples for the credit calc if procurement requests. See attached sla-exception-term-sheet.docx.

Thanks — see you on the call.

Best,
Kim
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Rao <samir@avatech.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Nov 2025 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Final: SLA exception addendum & next steps (DocuSign sent)

Samir / Team — following our call and procurement conversations, legal has approved the uplift term addendum with the stepped credit schedule and the 60/90-day windows as discussed. I just sent the DocuSign packet: https://www.docusign.com/placeholder/AVA-2025-1102

Next steps:
1) Ava signs the addendum in DocuSign (please route to Procurement + Legal).
2) We provision the additional GPUs within 7 business days of fully executed addendum.
3) Migration window: Redwood will schedule a warm-up run and cache prefill during the provisioning week; we'll coordinate a 48h maintenance window if needed.

If you need a worked example for the credit calculation, I can provide a spreadsheet showing the pro-rata credits on your current reserved monthly fee.

Thanks everyone — excited to get Ava scaled into Q1.

Marissa Cole
Director, Dedicated Accounts
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
